Rep. Van Epps’ Special America 250 Message | Congressman Matt Van Epps Skip to main content Rep. Van Epps’ Special America 250 Message July 2, 2026 Press Release Today, Rep. Van Epps released the following special message for the 250th anniversary of our nation’s founding. Also, in honor of America’s 250th anniversary, Rep. Van Epps introduced the  Declaration of Independence Reaffirmation Act of 2026.  You can read more about that  here or  here .   Watch the video by clicking below  Image Read excerpts from the video below: I was recently asked, “Do you think America lived up to what it set out to do 250 years ago?” My answer is a resounding yes!  Our Founding Fathers set out to found a new nation, one built on the principles of freedom, inalienable God-given rights, self-government, consent of the governed, and the right to make your own way—also known as the American Dream.  Today, the United States isn’t only one of the freest nations in the world, but we have also exported that freedom around the globe. This freedom empowers Americans to build and to innovate, to raise a family and to pursue what you’re passionate about. This freedom allows Americans to speak their minds, to worship without fear, and to keep the fruits of their labor.  Here in the United States, freedom isn’t an abstract idea, it's tangible. We see it when we choose where to send our kids to school, we hear it when we express our faith in public, and we taste it when we see our brave men and women fight for our flag wherever it is threatened.  250 years later, the United States continues to be the land of opportunity. And more people than ever before are achieving the American Dream.   So, Gold bless America and happy America 250th! Rep. Van Epps Announces 2026 Service Academy Day | Congressman Matt Van Epps Skip to main content Rep. Van Epps Announces 2026 Service Academy Day July 13, 2026 Press Release Rep. Van Epps Announces 2026 Service Academy Day Franklin, Tennessee - Rep. Matt Van Epps will host a Service Academy Day on Saturday, August 8, 2026, to provide students and families with information about the nation's prestigious U.S. Service Academies and Reserve Officers' Training Corps (ROTC) opportunities. Invited to attend the event are representatives from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point, the U.S. Naval Academy, the U.S. Air Force Academy, the U.S. Merchant Marine Academy, the U.S. Coast Guard Academy, and ROTC programs to answer questions about admissions, nominations, scholarships, and military service. Rep. Van Epps said, “My time at West Point shaped the leader I am today. Our service academies challenge young men and women to embrace duty, honor, and selfless service while preparing them to lead in uniform and beyond. Whether you're interested in attending a service academy or pursuing an ROTC scholarship, I encourage students and their families to join us to learn more about these life-changing opportunities to serve our country.” Service Academy Day Information: Date: Saturday, August 8, 2026 Doors Open: 10:00 a.m. Program: 10:30 a.m. - 1:30 p.m. Location: Franklin High School, 810 Hillsboro Road, Franklin, TN 37064 Students, parents, guidance counselors, and anyone interested in learning more about military service and academy admissions are encouraged to attend. Please RSVP for the Service Academy Day  here . For more information about the nomination process, visit Rep. Van Epps’ Service Academy FAQ page  here , or you can call his Franklin District office at (629) 223-6050.   To request a military service academy nomination from our office, please complete the form  here .  The deadline to apply is Thursday, October 30th, 2026, at 5:00 p.m.  For additional information, please contact Matthew Siciliano at matthew.siciliano@mail.house.gov. Like in the case of 18-year-old Sheridan Gorman––just this week, murdered by an illegal alien who shouldn’t have been here in the first place.  Her sister is a student at Vanderbilt University in my district. This family is suffering unimaginable loss and pain—and I’m sick of it.   And yet Democrats are still keeping DHS shut down––the very department in charge of protecting Americans at home.   Because of Democrats’ political games, TSA personnel have gone multiple pay periods without compensation. Van Epps Announces Mobile Office Hours for July and August July 24, 2026 Press Release Rep. Van Epps Announces Mobile Office Hours for July and August Franklin, TN – Rep. Van Epps’ district team will hold mobile office hours in communities across Tennessee’s 7th Congressional District throughout July and August. If you need assistance with a federal agency, our team will be available to help start a casework request and connect you with the appropriate federal resources. While Congressman Van Epps maintains district offices in Clarksville and Franklin, our team is committed to making constituent services accessible across the entire district. Through mobile office hours, staff members are able to meet Tennesseans closer to where they live and work, ensuring residents across TN-07 have direct access to assistance from their congressional office. If you need help with a federal agency but are unable to attend one of the mobile office hour events listed below, please contact our office at (629) 223-6050 or visit our website  here . Rep. Van Epps said , “From Montgomery County to Wayne County and from Benton County to Davidson County, I’ve had the opportunity to meet incredible Tennesseans across our district. One of my top priorities in Congress has been building a team that is responsive, accessible, and committed to serving the people of TN-07. Whether you need help with the Department of Veterans Affairs, the IRS, passport services, or another federal agency, our office is here to help. It would be our honor to serve you.”  Please come prepared to fill out a privacy release form, also found on the website  here !  Though Rep. Van Epps will not be at these mobile office hours, a member of his team will be! You can listen to a message from Rep. Rep. Van Epps Secures Major Legislative Victories in FY27 NDAA | Congressman Matt Van Epps Skip to main content Rep. Van Epps Secures Major Legislative Victories in FY27 NDAA July 22, 2026 Press Release Rep. Van Epps Secures Major Legislative Victories in FY27 NDAA Image WASHINGTON, D.C. - Rep. Matt Van Epps (TN-07) released the following statement after four of his amendments were included in the House’s version of the Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA).  HONOR Gold Star Families Act Amendment Rep. Van Epps stated , “I am proud that core provisions of my HONOR Gold Star Families Act made it into the FY27 NDAA. For the first time in nearly two decades, this legislation updates the military death gratuity by increasing the benefit for survivors from $100,000 to $165,000 and indexing future payments to inflation through a cost-of-living adjustment. This legislation will provide greater financial support to the families of fallen servicemembers who have sacrificed so much.”  Read more here .  Fort Campbell Water and Wastewater Infrastructure Amendment Rep. Van Epps said , “The fact of the matter is that aging water and wastewater infrastructure has become a growing concern for readiness and quality of life. Much of Fort Campbell’s utility system is more than 60 years old and requires significant maintenance and modernization to reduce the risk of service disruptions. Should a major disruption occur, it could affect everything from mission execution to the health of military families,” he continued .   He said , “Fort Campbell isn’t the only aging base. According to a 2024 CBO report , the four services have $50 billion in deferred maintenance on their bases, with the Army and Navy making up 70 percent of the backlog. Yet, despite the scale of the challenge, the Department of War (DOW) lacks a comprehensive assessment that identifies and prioritizes the military's most critical aging utility systems. That’s why I am introducing this amendment today.  My amendment directs the DOW to evaluate the condition, costs, and operational impacts of these systems across all military installations. Today, Rep. Van Epps Celebrates the Anniversary of NASA’s Founding | Congressman Matt Van Epps Skip to main content Today, Rep. Van Epps Celebrates the Anniversary of NASA’s Founding July 29, 2026 Press Release Today, Rep. Van Epps Celebrates the Anniversary of NASA’s Founding.  Today, Rep. Van Epps released the following message in celebration of NASA’s founding. As a member of the Science, Space, and Technology Committee, Rep. Van Epps is focused on ensuring the United States remains at the forefront of innovation, particularly in space technology. With an abundance of commercial investments in NASA and the space industry, Tennessee is helping lead the space race. Currently, Tennessee has $224.2 million in economic output due to NASA contracts alone. There are 26 Tennessee suppliers that contribute to NASA’s Artemis program, and more Tennessee companies support the Kennedy Space Center.  Image Watch Rep. Van Epps’ message by clicking above or here.  On July 29th, we celebrate the birthday of NASA, an agency that has embodied one of the most powerful qualities of the American spirit: the belief that there is always something greater ahead. For generations, NASA has reminded us of what is possible when Americans come together with a common purpose. It represents the dreamers who looked up at the night sky and wondered what lay beyond, the engineers who turned impossible ideas into reality, and the astronauts who climbed into rockets knowing they were carrying the hopes and aspirations of an entire nation. When Americans first reached the Moon, we did more than plant a flag. We showed what a free people can accomplish when we refuse to accept the impossible. That moment reflected something deeply woven into the American character. We are a nation of explorers. A nation of builders. A nation that has always looked beyond the horizon and asked, “What’s next?” The story of NASA is the story of American perseverance. Van Epps’ Major Non-NATO Ally Terror Threat Assessment Act July 13, 2026 Press Release House Passes Rep. Van Epps’ Major Non-NATO Ally Terror Threat Assessment Act  Washington, D.C.- Today, the House of Representatives passed Rep. Van Epps’ (TN07) Major Non-NATO Ally (MNNA)Terror Threat Assessment Act.   Upon passage of the bill, Rep. Van Epps stated, “I am grateful my Major Non-NATO Ally Terror Threat Assessment Act passed the House of Representatives today. When the United States designates a nation as a Major non-NATO ally, it's a significant move. Giving a country MNNA status is not merely symbolic; it comes with practical benefits, but also risks. This legislation strengthens coordination between the Department of Homeland Security and Congress to better assess and support MNNA partners as they confront terrorist threats within their own borders. This will ensure Congress has the information it needs to provide effective oversight as a partner with this administration.”  Watch or read Rep.
